newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Last prisoners leave South Africa's Robben Island.
newsitem.headline: Last prisoners leave South Africa's Robben Island.

text.p: Robben Island, where South African President Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in jail, was a place of freedom on Tuesday for the first time in three centuries.
Prison services spokesman Eddie Johnson said the last 92 prisoners were ferried off the island, 11 kilometres (7 miles) offshore in Cape Town's Table Bay, on Monday.
"The Correctional Services Department will hand the island over to the Department of Arts and Culture on the first of January," he said.

Robben Island, named for the seals hunted there by Dutch sailors on their way to the East, has been a place of exile, a leper colony or a prison constantly since Dutch settler Jan van Riebeeck marooned a troublesome interpreter known as Harry the Hottentot there in 1658.
Mandela's government announced in September that the island would become a freedom museum reflecting the various phases of colonisation and oppression in South Africa.
The government also intends to apply for recognition of the island, which measures 3.4 by 1.8 kilometres (2 by 1 miles), as a World Heritage site.

Visible from Cape Town as a sandy smudge on the northern horizon, the island became notorious after Mandela and his fellow conspirators were flown there in 1964 to begin life sentences for opposing white minority rule.
Mandela and his colleagues were forced to chip limestone in an island quarry, leaving him and others with permanent eye damage and other health problems.
Doctors say the tough conditions during the first decade of his imprisonment probably contributed to the knee problems that now cause Mandela to walk with visible difficulty.

The single-storey maximum-security prison housed close to 1,000 prisoners at its peak, but the last political detainees were taken off the island shortly before South Africa's white rulers handed power to the first democratic government in 1994.
Since then prison authorities have been slowly winding down to Tuesday's transfer of the remaining minor criminals on the island. The rest of the staff are scheduled to leave on New Year's Eve.
